title: Graph Representational Learning: When Does More Expressivity Hurt Generalization?
abstract: arXiv:2505.11298v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are powerful tools for learning on structured data, yet the relationship between their expressivity and predictive performance remains unclear. We introduce a family of premetrics that capture different degrees of structural similarity between graphs and relate these similarities to generalization, and consequently, the performance of expressive GNNs. By considering a setting where graph labels are correlated with structural features, we derive generalization bounds that depend on the distance between training and test graphs, model complexity, and training set size. These bounds reveal that more expressive GNNs may generalize worse unless their increased complexity is balanced by a sufficiently large training set or reduced distance between training and test graphs. Our findings relate expressivity and generalization, offering theoretical insights supported by empirical results.

translated_title: 图表示学习：更强的表达能力何时会损害泛化性能？
translated_abstract: 图神经网络是用于结构化数据学习的强大工具，但其表达能力与预测性能之间的关系仍不清楚。我们引入了一族预度量，用于刻画图之间不同程度的结构相似性，并将这些相似性与泛化能力联系起来，进而与表达能力强的图神经网络的性能相关联。通过考虑图标签与结构特征相关的设定，我们推导出了依赖于训练图与测试图之间的距离、模型复杂度以及训练集大小的泛化界。这些界表明，表达能力更强的图神经网络可能泛化性能更差，除非其增加的复杂度能够通过足够大的训练集或训练图与测试图之间距离的缩小来平衡。我们的发现将表达能力与泛化联系起来，提供了有实证结果支持的理论见解。
tldr: 本文引入一族刻画图结构相似性的预度量并推导出泛化界，揭示了表达能力更强的图神经网络可能泛化更差，只有当训练集足够大或训练图与测试图距离足够近时，更高的表达能力才不会损害泛化性能。
